notable_absence.predicate: requiresPrivilege / requiresCapellaRole / requiresEdition / availableSince / dependsOnService(index) / usesPort
notable_absence.finding: No access control of any kind, no edition gate, no version statement, no port, and no memory-quota figure - the same profile as search-service.md, so it is a property of the learn/services tree rather than of one page. Two absences are specific and worth SME attention. (1) The Analytics Service does not state its own Data Service dependency in dependency language. Its two sibling pages in the same directory both use the formula 'The X Service depends on the Data Service'; this page instead buries it inside a sentence about shadow collections. If the ontology is built by pattern-matching that formula, Analytics silently drops out of the dependency graph. (2) The Index Service dependency is stated ONLY on the parent services.md ('Creates indexes, for use by the Query and Analytics services') and nowhere on this page - recorded above as a cross-page relation with evidence_source rather than asserted from this page or dropped. Also absent: no statement of how many Analytics nodes are needed or supported, no mention of the 8-dataset ceiling that Capella's equivalent page states, and no definition of 'near real-time analytics' despite it being named as one of only two focus areas. I did not assert anything about dataset limits, replication, or Analytics-service scaling, because the page says nothing about any of them.

cross_component_finding: This page and search-service.md produced two OPPOSED deployment-topology constraints within one batch, and the registry had a predicate for neither: Search must be co-deployed with Query and Index for its SQL++ surface to work at all (requiresCoDeployedService), while Analytics should be deployed alone with no other service on its nodes (requiresDedicatedNode). That pair is the single clearest answer to this round's hypothesis - reference documentation produces gating axes (privilege, edition, credential type, UI mode, access surface) and conceptual documentation produces PLACEMENT axes, and the two vocabularies have no overlap. hasExecutionConstraint, the registry's one placement-flavoured predicate, was minted for 'every statement in a SQL++ transaction must be routed to the same Query node' - a request-routing rule, not a service-to-node allocation rule, so it does not cover either of these. Second cross-component point: 'shadow collections are connected to the Data Service ... using the Database Change Protocol' is the same mechanism search-service.md describes as 'the Data Service uses the DCP protocol to stream data-mutations'. Two pages in one directory, one protocol, two names, no cross-link, and no concept for it in the registry after nine rounds. Third: NUMA is the first time anything in the corpus has gated or degraded a Couchbase capability on the physical shape of the machine. The registry's behavesDifferentlyUnder axis has already been generalised to editions, deployments, cloud providers and storage engines; hardware topology would be a fifth, and I deliberately minted degradesPerformanceOf instead of adding it, because a performance warning is not a behavioural variation.
cross_product_finding: SAME SERVICE, TWO NAMES FOR ITS CENTRAL ARTIFACT. Capella's cloud/clusters/analytics-service/analytics-service.md calls the shadowed copy a 'dataset' (extracted as capella:analytics-dataset, 'a shadow copy of operational data ... up to 8 per cluster'); the self-managed page calls the identical thing a 'shadow copy' / 'shadow collection' and states no ceiling. These are one construct under two nouns, and nothing in either page connects them, so I minted analytics:shadow-collection rather than merging - but reconciliation should treat this as the batch's strongest merge candidate, on the same evidence standard the registry already applies to its collision writeups. Three further deployment-model divergences on the same service. (a) Capella's page states the dependency crisply ('The Analytics Service depends on the Data Service. This service must also be deployed on the cluster in order to use the Analytics Service.'); the self-managed page does not, which is the reverse of the expected direction - you would expect the self-managed tree to be the more architecturally explicit one. (b) Capella's page introduces analytics:sqlpp-for-analytics and capella:cost-based-optimizer-analytics as first-class Analytics concepts; the self-managed page never mentions that Analytics has its own SQL++ dialect at all, and links only to a generic 'Introduction to Couchbase Analytics'. (c) NUMA and dedicated-node placement cannot appear on Capella's side by construction - Capella chooses the hardware and the topology - so the two most substantive facts on this page are unstateable in the Capella tree. Net: for Analytics the self-managed page is richer on infrastructure and POORER on the service's own semantics than its Capella twin, and a merged ontology will show service:analytics-service with a hardware-and-placement fan from server/ and a language-and-optimizer fan from cloud/, with no page asserting they are one service.
